about.title: About the museum
about.lead: PLC Museum is an open, free, multilingual visual timeline of programmable logic controllers and distributed control systems, from 1969 to today.
about.audience: It is made for the engineers, technicians and operators who installed, programmed and kept these machines running, and for anyone curious about how industrial automation came to be.
about.sources_body: Every specification, date and claim is backed by a recorded source: manuals, datasheets, vendor histories, books, period articles or recorded interviews. When a fact has no source yet, the page says so instead of guessing.
about.licenses_body: The code is under the MIT license. Catalog content and original illustrations are under CC BY 4.0. Photographs appear only with a recorded license or written permission, and each one is credited next to the image.
about.independent_body: The museum has no affiliation with any manufacturer. Product and company names appear as text, for identification and historical description only, and no logos are used.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: This site sets no cookies, does not track you and loads no third-party scripts.
privacy.hosting: The museum is a set of static pages hosted on Cloudflare. Like any web host, Cloudflare processes technical data such as your IP address to deliver the pages and to protect the site against abuse.
privacy.no_forms: There are no forms and no accounts. The museum does not collect, store or sell personal data.
privacy.stories: Field story submissions will open later. Before they do, this page will carry their full privacy notice: what is collected, why, for how long, and how to have it removed.
credits.title: Credits
credits.lead: The museum is a community effort. These are the works and people it depends on.
credits.illustrations: Original illustrations are drawn for the museum and published under CC BY 4.0.
credits.photos: Photographs are credited next to each image, with their author and license recorded in the repository.
credits.contributors: Contributors are credited by their GitHub handle.
credits.contributors_link: See everyone who contributed on GitHub
contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.lead: The museum grows with the memory of the people who worked with these machines.
contribute.later: The field story form opens later. Until then, you can help through the GitHub repository:
contribute.exhibits: Propose an exhibit, with a source for every fact.
contribute.corrections: Correct a fact, citing the source that supports the change.
contribute.photos: Offer a photograph you took, or one you have written permission to share, together with its license.
contribute.translations: Review a translation into your language, if you are a native speaker who knows the shop floor jargon.
